beats.label: S1 · Picard's exile
beats.text: Rogue synths attacked Mars during Picard's Romulan rescue effort. Starfleet abandoned the refugees and banned synthetics; Picard resigned in disgust and retired to his vineyard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Picard's guilt, Starfleet's compromised state, and the synth ban that everything else pivots on.

beats.label: S1 · Data's daughter
beats.text: A woman named Dahj finds Picard, hunted by Romulan assassins who kill her. He learns she was Data's synthetic daughter, and has a twin, Soji, on a decommissioned Borg Cube.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the mission target and Data's legacy, the personal debt driving Picard out of retirement.

beats.label: S1 · The new crew
beats.text: Picard gathers a crew — pilot Rios, ex-officer Raffi, roboticist Jurati, and Romulan warrior Elnor — to find Soji before the assassins do.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This ensemble persists into the next season; the reader must know who these people are and how they came to serve Picard.

beats.label: S1 · The Zhat Vash
beats.text: The killers are Zhat Vash, a Romulan cult convinced synthetic life ends all life. Their leader Commodore Oh has infiltrated Starfleet and engineered the Mars attack herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the antagonist and reveals the synth ban itself was manufactured — reframes Starfleet's failure as sabotage from within.

beats.label: S1 · Jurati's betrayal
beats.text: Oh compels Jurati to kill Soji's creator Bruce Maddox and track the crew from within. Guilt breaks Jurati before she can finish the job, and she confesses everything.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jurati's guilt and the murder of Maddox define who she is at season's end — a repentant killer who chose the crew over her handler.

beats.label: S1 · Coppelius
beats.text: On Soji's home planet Coppelius, she begins summoning the very synthetic armada Zhat Vash prophecy feared. Picard talks her down, dying of his terminal illness as he does.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central conflict resolves through persuasion, not force, and costs Picard his life — setting up his transformation.

beats.label: S1 · A second life
beats.text: Picard's mind is transferred into a synthetic body Maddox had prepared, indistinguishable from his own. The synth ban is lifted, and the crew scatters to new lives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Picard is now literally what he fought for. Everything about him going forward is coloured by his synthetic body and second chance.

cliffhanger.text: Picard walks out of death in a synthetic body, the synth ban lifted and the Zhat Vash exposed. His crew disperses across the quadrant, each carrying their own unfinished business.
questions: What does Picard do with a second life he never expected?
Where do Rios, Raffi, Seven, Elnor, and Jurati end up now that the mission is done?
Is a Federation that once turned on its own really rebuilt, or just papered over?

characters.name: Jean-Luc Picard
characters.line: Retired Starfleet admiral, killed on Coppelius and resurrected into a synthetic body indistinguishable from his own.

characters.name: Soji Asha
characters.line: Data's synthetic daughter, freed from Romulan captivity and now living among her own kind on Coppelius.

characters.name: Dr. Agnes Jurati
characters.line: Daystrom roboticist who murdered Bruce Maddox under Zhat Vash coercion, confessed to the crew, and awaits Starfleet judgment.

characters.name: Chris Rios
characters.line: Freelance captain of La Sirena and ex-Starfleet, haunted by a former captain who killed synths on a Federation cover-up.

characters.name: Raffi Musiker
characters.line: Ex-Starfleet officer fired after the Mars attack, back in the fight through Picard and estranged from her son Gabriel.

characters.name: Elnor
characters.line: Young Romulan warrior of the Qowat Milat, raised in exile after Picard abandoned Vashti and now his sworn protector.

characters.name: Seven of Nine
characters.line: Former Borg drone and Fenris Ranger vigilante, allied with Picard after connecting with the reclaimed Borg Cube.

characters.name: Laris
characters.line: Picard's Romulan housekeeper and former Tal Shiar operative, running the vineyard alongside her partner Zhaban.

beats.label: S2 · A life half-lived
beats.text: A year and a half after Zhaban's death, Picard gently rejects his housekeeper Laris's advances. Now Starfleet Academy chancellor, he remains unable to open himself to love.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the season's actual subject — Picard's fear of intimacy — which the Q trial exists to interrogate.

beats.label: S2 · Borg incursion
beats.text: An anomaly asks to join the Federation. A Borg Queen emerges and begins assimilating the fleet; Picard triggers self-destruct and wakes in a fascist Confederation timeline.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The inciting break in reality that launches the entire season's plot and reunites the scattered crew.

beats.label: S2 · Q's final trial
beats.text: Q reveals this reality is his final test of Picard. The crew captures the alt-Borg Queen and slingshots to 2024 Los Angeles, where a single event apparently ruined the future.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the antagonist, the destination, and the mission — the frame the rest of the season hangs on.

beats.label: S2 · Crash in 2024
beats.text: They crash near Chateau Picard. Elnor dies of his wounds, the Queen fades to a shell, and they must locate the Watcher who guards whatever event will change history.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Elnor's death drives Raffi's arc; the crippled Queen and the search for the Watcher structure the middle stretch.

beats.label: S2 · Renée and Soong
beats.text: The Watcher is Tallinn, protecting Picard's ancestor Renée whose Europa mission will change everything. Q recruits geneticist Adam Soong to stop her from ever flying.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Identifies the pivot point of history and the human weapon Q aims at it — the season's central conflict.

beats.label: S2 · A new Queen
beats.text: The dying Queen infects Jurati with nanoprobes. Jurati persuades her to reject assimilation, and the two merge into a new, benevolent Borg Queen who departs for the Delta Quadrant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jurati's fate closes her S1 guilt arc and establishes a new kind of Borg — a peaceable faction now watching from afar.

beats.label: S2 · Farewell
beats.text: Tallinn dies saving Renée from Soong's attack. A dying Q sends Picard home, and Picard — having learned to accept love — finally asks Laris for a second chance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves Q, the timeline, and Picard's emotional block; leaves Picard partnered with Laris going into the next chapter.

cliffhanger.text: Picard is home with Elnor alive, Laris waiting, and Q apparently dead. Jurati's benevolent Borg join the Federation as provisional members, watching a newly detected trans-warp conduit.
questions: Can Picard finally live the quiet life he denied himself?
What is coming through the trans-warp conduit Jurati's Borg have found?
Where does the scattered crew go now that Q's trial is over?

characters.name: Jean-Luc Picard
characters.line: Starfleet Academy chancellor in his synthetic body, finally opening himself to love with Laris.

characters.name: Laris
characters.line: Picard's Romulan housekeeper, widowed a year earlier — her advances first rejected, then answered on Picard's return.

characters.name: Chris Rios
characters.line: Former captain of the USS Stargazer who chose to remain in 21st-century Earth with clinic doctor Teresa.

characters.name: Dr. Agnes Jurati
characters.line: Merged with the dying Borg Queen to become a new, benevolent Borg Queen leading a cooperative collective.

characters.name: Seven of Nine
characters.line: Vigilante pilot of La Sirena, her Borg damage healed by the new Queen; back in an on-again bond with Raffi.

characters.name: Raffi Musiker
characters.line: Officer aboard the USS Excelsior, mentoring Elnor at the Academy after grieving his death in the alt-timeline.

characters.name: Elnor
characters.line: Starfleet Academy cadet under Picard, killed in the alternate timeline but restored when history was set right.

characters.name: Q
characters.line: Extra-dimensional being who spent his last power on Picard's trial and apparently died to teach him to let go.

beats.label: S3 · The distress signal
beats.text: Dr. Beverly Crusher sends a distress signal after twenty years' silence. Picard and Riker rescue her adult son Jack, whom Picard belatedly realises is his own child.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Announces the season's premise — Beverly's return, a hidden son, and a threat serious enough to break twenty years of silence.

beats.label: S3 · Vadic's hunt
beats.text: A bounty hunter, Vadic, pursues Jack aboard her ship the Shrike. She corners the USS Titan under Captain Shaw; the crew barely escapes into a nebula and are forced to fight back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the primary antagonist and traps the ensemble on one ship, focusing the season on Jack as the target.

beats.label: S3 · Ro's warning
beats.text: Commander Ro Laren reveals Changeling shapeshifters have infiltrated Starfleet's highest levels. She dies detonating her shuttle against a compromised Starfleet ship to save the Titan.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes Vadic's hunt as one front of a much wider conspiracy — the real enemy is inside Starfleet itself.

beats.label: S3 · The old crew
beats.text: Picard's Enterprise-D crew regroups. At Daystrom Station they recover a synthetic body carrying Data's mind alongside Lore's, and Geordi restores Data to full consciousness.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reunites the TNG ensemble and resurrects Data — the emotional core of the finale and the crew who ultimately win the day.

beats.label: S3 · Jack's secret
beats.text: Changelings stole Picard's original body to harvest dormant Borg tissue he unknowingly passed to Jack. The crew defeats Vadic aboard the Titan, but the true plan is already unfolding.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals what the Changelings actually want and that Jack is the delivery mechanism — collapses the two mysteries into one.

beats.label: S3 · Frontier Day
beats.text: On Frontier Day the Borg Queen uses Jack to assimilate every young Starfleet officer through the transporter network, seizing the fleet. Only Geordi's restored Enterprise-D is free.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The catastrophe the season has been building toward; strips the Federation to nothing and puts the old crew on the only functional ship.

beats.label: S3 · The last generation
beats.text: The Enterprise-D destroys the Queen's cube and frees Jack. A year later the Titan is rechristened Enterprise-G under Captain Seven, and a supposedly dead Q quietly appears to Jack.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Borg threat, hands the future to a new generation, and plants Q's return to Jack as the door the show leaves open.

cliffhanger.text: The Borg and Changeling threats are broken and the Enterprise-D crew are back in their places. But Q — thought dead — has appeared to Ensign Jack Crusher, announcing that his trial has just begun.
questions: What trial does Q have in store for Jack?
Is Q truly dead, or simply moved on to a new subject?
Can Jack's Borg-touched mind ever be truly free?

characters.name: Jean-Luc Picard
characters.line: Retired admiral pulled back into service by Beverly's call, now father to a grown son and reunited with his old crew.

characters.name: Dr. Beverly Crusher
characters.line: The Enterprise-D's former CMO, who vanished with Jack for twenty years to keep Picard's enemies away from their child.

characters.name: Jack Crusher
characters.line: Picard and Beverly's grown son, marked by dormant Borg tissue inherited from his father, now a Starfleet ensign.

characters.name: William Riker
characters.line: Picard's oldest friend and former first officer, briefly commanded the Titan during the Changeling crisis.

characters.name: Deanna Troi
characters.line: Riker's wife and Betazoid empath, helped Jack surface the Borg voices calling to him from within.

characters.name: Seven of Nine
characters.line: Former Titan first officer, promoted to Captain of the newly rechristened USS Enterprise-G.

characters.name: Raffi Musiker
characters.line: Starfleet intelligence officer who uncovered the Changeling plot, now first officer of the Enterprise-G.

characters.name: Worf
characters.line: Klingon warrior turned Starfleet intelligence operative, Raffi's handler on the Changeling case.

characters.name: Geordi La Forge
characters.line: Commodore in charge of the Starfleet Museum; secretly restored the Enterprise-D and revived Data.

characters.name: Data
characters.line: Picard's late android friend, resurrected in a new synthetic body after subsuming his brother Lore.
